The provided image displays two line plots comparing the performance of two models, "Llama-On-Policy" and "Llama-LUFFY," across different training set difficulties: "Easy" and "Hard." Each plot illustrates how the models' performance evolves over the number of training steps, with the x-axis labeled "Steps" and the y-axis representing performance metrics (though the specific unit is not labeled). Both plots use a linear scale for the x-axis, which spans from 0 to approximately 100,000 steps, with tick marks appearing at regular intervals (e.g., every 20,000 steps). The y-axis also uses a linear scale, though its exact range and units are not specified.

In the top plot, labeled "Easy Training Set," the blue line ("Llama-On-Policy-Easy") begins at a lower performance value (around 0.3) and rises to a plateau near 0.95. The red line ("Llama-LUFFY-Easy") starts at a higher value (around 0.5) and follows a similar upward trend, reaching a plateau near 0.98. Both lines exhibit some fluctuation around their final plateau values.

In the bottom plot, labeled "Hard Training Set," the blue line ("Llama-On-Policy-Hard") begins at a very low value (near 0.0) and shows a slow, steady increase to approximately 0.5. The red line ("Llama-LUFFY-Hard") starts at a slightly higher value (around 0.1) and increases more rapidly, reaching a plateau near 0.95. Both lines show some variability around their final values, with the red line demonstrating a more pronounced upward trend compared to the blue line.
